Ichijou was still boiling.

Perhaps my earlier warning was still operating somewhere inside her, because she was not raising her voice. Even so, displeasure was seeping out of her from head to foot.

This was one of the roads leading from the main keep down to the second bailey, where the officials' quarters stood. The slope was steep; perhaps that was why there were no other passersby. I had chosen it hoping for exactly that, and for once the judgment had been rewarded.

Even so.

en.html:
I reconfirmed the policy I had held from the very beginning.

Taking our time would only lead us to self-destruction, and that was not Ichijou's fault alone. I, too, am not made for something as delicate as infiltration work. The cracks would show soon enough. So the answer was to finish the job quickly, before they did, and leave. For a pair like Ichijou and me, there was no better way.

Since we had given up careful preparation, a very rough plan could not be avoided. But the Prince must have known that from the start. In fact, he wanted a certain degree of roughness.

He had gone out of his way to send two warriors, to slap the swollen face of arrogant Rokuhara and, in the same stroke, to show our ally Raichou Imagawa some strength. It is not as if he lacked specialist agents.

The real problem was how to turn the Prince Maidono's wish into a concrete plan...

en.html:
Young. Beautiful also, it seemed.

That was no reason for suspicion. This royal castle must hold any number of women who meet the same two conditions.

That a woman should choose such a steep path was odd, I grant, but not odd enough to raise an alarm. Ichijou herself was walking it without any trouble.

And yet, as a fact, this woman had caught my attention.

It was not because of eccentric dress. Her clothes were very plain... plain in a different way from the functional uniforms of officials, like Ms Iwata's.

Nor were they a menial's clothes.

In the end, perhaps that was where the snag lay.

Clothes announce a person's rank and position. On this woman they announced neither.

Her features had breeding. Judged by the face alone, she might be the daughter of a great house. Add the clothes, and plainly no. She did not look like a lady serving in the inner quarters, or a shrine maiden at the castle shrine, or a clerk, or a soldier, or a sweeper, or the person who cooks the rice in the canteen.

This castle is a small society in which every person's rank and duty has been fixed with great strictness. And she fitted into none of the boxes.

She was out of place, and visibly so: first her figure, then her air of having nowhere to be, which only made it worse.

ja.html:
若い。美しいようにも見える。
　しかしそれは別段、訝しむに値しない。同様の条件
に該当する女性はこの王城にいくらもいるだろう。

　女の身でわざわざ、こんな険しい道を選んで歩くの
は奇異といえば奇異だが……
　それも怪しむほどの事ではない。一条とて、何の苦
もなく歩んでいる。

　にも拘わらず事実として、その女性は注意を引いた。

　奇抜な格好をしているという事もない。
　ごく、素朴な装束だ……岩田女史のような、役人用
の機能的なものとはまた違う種の。

　といって、雑用婦の身なりでもない。
　
　結局、そこが引っ掛かるのか。

　服装はその人の身分、立場を表すものだ。
　が、女性の格好からはそれが見えない。

　容貌には気品があり、その点のみ見れば権門の姫と
も思える。しかし服装を含めれば明らかに違う。
　奥で奉仕する女官にも城内の神社の<ruby>巫<rt>かんなぎ</rt></ruby>にも役人にも
武官にも掃除人にも食堂の飯炊きにも見えない。

　この城内は人間の階級と役割が厳格に規定された小
社会を構成している。なのにその何処にも該当しない。
　浮いているのだった。その姿が――所在無げな態度
も含めて。

en.html:
Only a few seconds passed between starting the thought and acting on it. There was hesitation, all the same.

As a Rokuhara official, I ought not to overlook a suspicious woman. But she might not be suspicious at all. She might be a person of some special standing whom every resident of the castle knows. In that case, ignorance on my part could prove fatal. "I am new here" would not necessarily save me.

In the end, though, this was the side on which I put my wooden counter.

en.html:
The Okabe princess said it without any feeling.

For a while I had no words to continue with. Ichijou, too, had gone silent.

I quietly kicked away the fallen stick at Ichijou's feet, which, of all the directions available, was pointing west, toward the cliff, and began fitting the pieces in my head together.

...I see. So that was why she looked so out of place.

Yoritsuna Okabe. A man whose power had once matched Moriuji Ashikaga's, who had even obtained the post of Director of the Board of Censors, an office normally given to imperial princes.

His daughter.

Born of a famous house, she could not now have that fame recognized in public. Noble, but stripped of wealth. And neither could she find a place among the commoners.

As she herself said, she was the seed of a defeated general and nothing else.

Of course she stood out in this castle.

　本人の語る通り、ただ敗将の胤であり、それ以外の
何者でも有り得ない。
　この城にあって存在が際立つのは当然だった。

Sakurako"Please forgive me... But what unusual people you are."
Kageaki"If you would be kind enough not to judge our whole character by the scene just now, I would not be at all unwilling to feel deep gratitude."

Kageaki"This girl is strange. I am normal."

Sakurako"Yes. You do not feel very... real."

en.html:
The princess imitated Ichijou's tone, playfully.

I was in no condition to laugh.

An arrow shot blind had gone through the center of the target. The princess clearly meant nothing by it, but staying fully calm was impossible.

Somehow, I pushed the surprise back down before it reached my face. Ichijou, too, held on, letting out only a tiny sound like a hiccup.

en.html:
Kageaki"...Before this, I did clerical work in the countryside. By some chance I was promoted to this place, and honestly I am mostly confused."
Sakurako"Is that so...? Then you must have many worries."
Sakurako"I cannot compare myself with people like you, who work properly, but... In an unfamiliar place, many things are difficult."
Kageaki"Indeed..."
Sakurako"The complicated roads are the worst of it. At Sasagawa I had watchers following me all the time. It is good not to have that here, but losing my way every time I step outside is quite unbearable."

en.html:
Fortresses, and not only Fudaraku, often have road systems more tangled than they need to be.

The purpose is to delay an enemy even slightly once the gates are broken, and to split up his forces.

Naturally, the same layout lets people who know it travel between key points in the least possible time... A lady who had lived in the castle for one week could hardly be blamed for not knowing it.
